items.stem:
Raju is a design engineer at a large pharmacy company. He has to decide the shape of medicine and for this he has to chose between tablet or captab.
a. Tablet : This is circular tablet.
b. Captab : This is long tablet having semicircular at both end.
The volume of medicine is 924 mm³.
(i) If Raju decide to make tablet of diameter 14 mm, what is the thickness of tablet ?
(ii) If Raju decide to make captab of dimension 7 by 23.5 mm, what is the thickness of captab ?
items.answer:
(i) The tablet is a circular disc. Its flat face is a circle of diameter 14 mm, so radius 7 mm, and its area is S = π(d/2)² = (22/7) × 7² = 154 mm². A disc of face area S and thickness t has volume S × t, so 924 = 154 × t, giving t = 924 ÷ 154 = 6 mm.
(ii) The captab is 23.5 mm long and 7 mm wide with a semicircle at each end, so its face is a rectangle of length 23.5 − 7 = 16.5 mm and width 7 mm, capped by two semicircles of radius 3.5 mm (one full circle between them). Face area = π(7/2)² + 16.5 × 7 = (22/7) × (49/4) + 115.5 = 38.5 + 115.5 = 154 mm². Then 924 = 154 × t, so t = 6 mm.
Both the tablet and the captab must be 6 mm thick.
items.ocr: The book prints 'The volume of medicine is 924 mm²'; a volume cannot be in mm², and the worked solution uses 924 mm³ throughout, so the stem is written with mm³. The solution likewise prints 'volume of captab must be 924 mm²'. The captab diagram (23.5 overall, 16.5 rectangle, 7 width) is drawn inside the solution, so it is not attached to the question.

items.stem:
Silo : A silo is a structure for storing bulk materials. Silos are used in agriculture to store grain or fermented feed known as silage. Silos are commonly used for bulk storage of grain, coal, cement, carbon black, woodchips, food products and sawdust.
A silo is in the shape of cylinder surmounted by a conical top. The height and diameter of cylindrical part are 40 feet and 42 feet respectively and the slant height of conical part is 29 feet.
(i) How much metal sheet is required to make this silo ?
(ii) Find the cost of metal sheet needed to make the silo if the metal sheet is available at the rate of Rs. 250 per square feet.
(iii) What is the storage capacity of silo ?
items.answer:
The cylinder and the cone share the radius r = 42 ÷ 2 = 21 feet. The cylinder's height is h_cy = 40 feet and the cone's slant height is l = 29 feet, so the cone's height is h_co = √(29² − 21²) = √(841 − 441) = √400 = 20 feet.
(i) Only the curved faces are covered by sheet, since the cone sits on the cylinder and the base rests on the ground: S = πrl + 2πrh_cy = πr(l + 2h_cy) = (22/7) × 21 × (29 + 80) = 66 × 109 = 7194 square feet.
(ii) At Rs. 250 per square foot the cost is 7194 × 250 = Rs. 17,98,500.
(iii) Capacity = volume of cylinder + volume of cone = πr²h_cy + (1/3)πr²h_co = (22/7) × 21² × (40 + 20/3) = 1386 × 140/3 = 64680 cubic feet.
items.ocr: Two printed answers conflict with the question and with the solution's own working. (a) The stem says Rs. 250 per square feet but the solution computes 7194 × 125 = 899250; the answer above follows the printed rate of 250, giving Rs. 17,98,500. (b) The solution reaches '= 22 × 21 × 140' and then prints '= 61600 feet³'; 22 × 21 × 140 = 64680, so 64680 cubic feet is used. The silo diagram is drawn inside the solution, so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
Rainfall is one of the most commonly shared experiences on Earth. Rainfall is also necessary, since it provides water to plants and ultimately fills rivers. Because rainfall is both a needed resources and a threat, it is important to better understand this natural phenomenon. The most common rainfall measurement is the total rainfall depth during a given period, expressed in millimetres (mm). For instance, we might want to know how many millimetres of rain fell over the course of 1 h, 1 day, 1 month, or 1 year.
The rain water from 22 m × 20 m roof drains into cylindrical vessel of diameter 2 m and height 3.5 m.
(i) If the rain water collected from the roof fills 4/5 of cylindrical vessel then find the rainfall in cm.
(ii) If rainfall is the 1.5 cm find the height of water collected in cylindrical vessel.
items.answer:
The vessel has radius r = 2/2 = 1 m and height 3.5 m.
(i) Water collected = (4/5)πr²h = (4/5) × (22/7) × 1² × (7/2) = 44/5 m³. The rain falling on the roof to depth h metres has volume 22 × 20 × h, so 440h = 44/5, giving h = 1/50 m = 2 cm. The rainfall is 2 cm.
(ii) A rainfall of 1.5 cm = 0.015 m over the roof gives 22 × 20 × 0.015 = 6.6 m³. If h₁ is the depth in the vessel, πr²h₁ = 6.6, so (22/7) × 1² × h₁ = 6.6 and h₁ = 6.6 × 7 ÷ 22 = 2.1 m. The water stands 2.1 m deep in the vessel.
items.ocr: The book prints the fraction as '4th/5', which is 4/5; and 'hight' for height in part (ii). The house illustration is decorative — every measurement the question needs is in the text — so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
Rain Water Harvesting : Water harvesting is the activity of direct collection of rainwater, rather than allowing it to run off. The rainwater collected can be stored for direct use or can be recharged into the groundwater.
Rajkumar has installed rain water harvesting system in his house. His has a roof with dimensions shown below. He knows that the average rainfall in his suburb is 77 cm per year. Rajkumar would like to install a underground cylindrical rain water tank to hold the water that runs off the roof.
Can you help the Rajkumar answer the following questions
(i) On average what volume of water will fall on the roof each year ?
(ii) How many litres of water does the tank need to hold?
(iii) If the tank has base diameter 7 m, how deep it need to be?
(iv) What is the inner surface area of the tank ?
items.answer:
Rain is caught by the plan area the roof covers, not by its sloping faces. The roof is 50 m long, rises 5 m to the ridge, and each sloping face measures 13 m across, so half the base width is √(13² − 5²) = √(169 − 25) = 12 m and the full width is w = 24 m.
(i) Base area = 24 × 50 = 1200 m². A yearly rainfall of 77 cm = 0.77 m gives a volume of 1200 × 0.77 = 924 m³.
(ii) Since 1 m³ = 1000 litres, the tank must hold 924 × 1000 = 9,24,000 litres.
(iii) The tank has radius r = 7/2 = 3.5 m. From πr²h = 924, (22/7) × (7/2)² × h = 924, so 38.5h = 924 and h = 24 m deep.
(iv) Inner curved surface S = 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × (7/2) × 24 = 528 m².
items.ocr: The roof's dimensions (13, 5, 50 and the unknown w) appear only in the printed diagram, so the diagram is attached — the question cannot be answered without it. Part (iv) is answered as the book does, as the curved surface alone.

items.stem:
Advertising columns are cylindrical outdoor sidewalk structures with a characteristic style that are used for advertising and other purposes. They are common throughout Germany including its capital Berlin, where the first 100 columns were installed in 1855. Advertising columns are typically used to display advertisements in the form of posters, traditionally chiefly theatre, cinema, nightclub, and concert announcements. Some are motorized and rotate very slowly.
Rajesh has been given the task of designing a advertising column for a client. It consist of a cylindrical part surmounted by hemisphere part on top. The base diameter of column is 7 feet and height of cylindrical part is 11 feet.
(i) Find the surface area of cylindrical part of column?
(ii) Find the total surface area of advertising column?
(iii) If cost of construction of column is Rs 75 per sq feet, find the total cost of a column.
(iv) Find the volume of advertising column ?
items.answer:
The cylinder and the hemisphere share the radius r = 7/2 = 3.5 feet, and the cylinder's height is h = 11 feet.
(i) Curved surface of the cylindrical part = 2πrh = 2 × (22/7) × 3.5 × 11 = 242 square feet.
(ii) The hemisphere caps the cylinder, so its flat face is hidden and only its curved surface 2πr² shows: total = 242 + 2 × (22/7) × 3.5² = 242 + 77 = 319 square feet.
(iii) Cost = 319 × 75 = Rs. 23,925.
(iv) Volume = πr²h + (2/3)πr³ = πr²(h + 2r/3) = (22/7) × 3.5² × (11 + 7/3) = 38.5 × 40/3 = 513.33 cubic feet.
items.concept: Solids in daily life are combinations
items.ocr: The photograph of a Berlin column is decorative; both dimensions the question needs are in the text, so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
Amul Dairy : Over the years, Amul, one of the most beloved brands of our country, has become the taste of India, just as its tagline claims. Every Indian millennial has grown up listening to the jingles of its many dairy products, and the Amul girl, the brand's mascot in the polka-dotted dress, has become a nostalgia-evoking symbol. Amul has truly come a long way since its founding in 1946.
A milk tanker of Amul diary, cylindrical in shape having diameter 2 m and length 4.2 m supplies milk to the two booths in the ratio of 3 : 2. One of the milk booths has cuboidal vessel having base area 3.96 sq. m. and the other has a cylindrical vessel having radius 1 m. Use π = 22/7.
(i) What is the volume of milk tanker ?
(ii) Find the level of milk in cuboidal vessel ?
(iii) How much milk is supplied to cylindrical vessel ?
(iv) Find the level of milk in cylindrical vessel ?
items.answer:
(i) The tanker is a cylinder lying on its side, of radius R = 2/2 = 1 m and length L = 4.2 m, so V = πR²L = (22/7) × 1² × 4.2 = 13.2 m³.
(ii) The first booth receives 3/5 of the milk: 13.2 × 3/5 = 7.92 m³. Its vessel is a cuboid of base area 3.96 m², so the milk stands 7.92 ÷ 3.96 = 2 m deep.
(iii) The second booth receives 2/5 of the milk: 13.2 × 2/5 = 5.28 m³.
(iv) That vessel is a cylinder of radius 1 m, base area π(1)² = 22/7 m². Level = 5.28 ÷ (22/7) = 5.28 × 7 ÷ 22 = 1.68 m.
items.ocr: The photograph of Amul products and the milk-tanker cartoon are decorative; every measurement is given in the text, so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
Suppose a sugar cone is 10 centimeters deep and has a diameter of 4 centimeters. A spherical scoop of ice cream with a diameter of 4 centimeters rests on the top of the cone.
(i) If all the ice cream melts into the cone, will the cone overflow? Explain.
(ii) If the cone does not overflow, what percent of the cone will be filled?
items.answer:
The cone and the scoop share the radius r = 4/2 = 2 cm; the cone's depth is h = 10 cm.
(i) Volume of the cone = (1/3)πr²h = (1/3)π(2)²(10) = 41.9 cm³. Volume of the spherical scoop = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3)π(2)³ = 33.5 cm³. Since 33.5 cm³ is less than 41.9 cm³, the melted ice cream fits and the cone will not overflow.
(ii) Fraction filled = 33.5 ÷ 41.9 = 0.80, so the cone will be about 80% filled.
items.ocr: The photograph of ice cream cones is decorative; both diameters and the depth are stated in the text, so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
Earth, the third planet from the sun, is the fifth-largest planet in the solar system The radius of Earth at the equator is 3,963 miles (6,378 kilometers), according to NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center in Greenbelt, Maryland. However, Earth is not quite a sphere. The planet's rotation causes it to bulge at the equator. Earth's polar radius is 3,950 miles (6,356 km) — a difference of 13 miles (22 km).
The diameter of Earth is d₁ miles from the North Pole to the South Pole and d₂ miles from opposite points at the equator.
(i) Find the surface area of Earth using each measure.
(ii) About 75% of Earth's surface is covered by water. Find the surface area of water on Earth, using the mean of the two diameters.
(iii) If the atmosphere of Earth extends to about 100 miles above the surface, find the surface area of the atmosphere surrounding Earth. Use the mean of the two diameters.
(iv) Find the volume of the atmosphere surrounding Earth using the mean of the two diameters.
items.answer:
A sphere of diameter d has surface area 4πr² = πd² and volume (4/3)πr³ = (1/6)πd³.
(i) Pole to pole the surface area is T = πd₁²; across the equator it is T = πd₂².
(ii) The mean diameter is d = ½(d₁ + d₂). Water covers 75% of the surface, so its area is 0.75πd² = (3/4) × (22/7) × ¼(d₁ + d₂)² = (33/56)(d₁ + d₂)² square miles.
(iii) The atmosphere reaches 100 miles above the surface all round, so its diameter is 200 miles more than the mean: 200 + ½(d₁ + d₂). Its surface area is T = π[200 + ½(d₁ + d₂)]² = (π/4)(400 + d₁ + d₂)².
(iv) The atmosphere is the shell between the two spheres: V = (1/6)π[200 + ½(d₁ + d₂)]³·(8/8) − (1/6)π[½(d₁ + d₂)]³, and writing each cube over 8 gives V = (π/48)[(400 + d₁ + d₂)³ − (d₁ + d₂)³] cubic miles.
items.ocr: In part (iv) the book's last line prints (1/48)π[(200 + d₁ + d₂)³ − (d₁ + d₂)³], but the line above it correctly sets up (1/6)π[200 + ½(d₁+d₂)]³ − (1/6)π[½(d₁+d₂)]³, which factors to (π/48)[(400 + d₁ + d₂)³ − (d₁ + d₂)³] — the same 400 the book itself reaches in part (iii). The corrected form is given. The globe cartoon is decorative, so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
Mother's Day is a celebration honouring the mother of the family or individual, as well as motherhood, maternal bonds, and the influence of mothers in society. It is celebrated on different days in many parts of the world, most commonly in the month of May.
India today did a survey among children for the amount of time spend with mothers. The result of survey is shown in figure. Suppose the bubble in the graphic is a sphere with a radius of 21 cm.
(i) What is the volume of the bubble?
(ii) What is the volume of the portion of the bubble in which the kids had just the right amount of time with their mother?
(iii) What is the surface area of the portion of the bubble in which the kids had wish for more amount of time with their mother?
(iv) What is the area of the two-dimensional sector of the circle in which the kids wish they could spend less time with their mother?
items.answer:
The bubble is a sphere of radius r = 21 cm, and the survey splits it into 60% 'just right', 30% 'wish for more time' and 10% 'wish for less time'.
(i) V = (4/3)πr³ = (4/3) × (22/7) × 21³ = 4 × 22 × 21 × 21 = 38808 cm³.
(ii) The 'just right' share is 60%: 38808 × 0.6 = 23284.8 cm³.
(iii) Total surface area T = 4πr² = 4 × (22/7) × 21² = 5544 cm². The 'wish for more' share is 30%: 5544 × 0.3 = 1663.2 cm².
(iv) The flat circle has area A = πr² = (22/7) × 21² = 1386 cm². The 'wish for less' sector is 10%: 1386 × 0.1 = 138.6 cm².
items.ocr: The three percentages (10%, 30%, 60%) are printed only inside the survey graphic, so the graphic is attached. The book misnumbers the third sub-part as '(ii)'; it is written as (iii) here. In the solution the book computes 5544 × 0.3 = 1663.2 cm² and then states the answer as 'approximately 1163 mm²' — the computed 1663.2 cm² is used. The book also prints cm² for the volume in (ii) and mm² for the area in (iv); these are cm³ and cm² respectively.

items.stem:
Pantheon : The Pantheon is the best-preserved building from ancient Rome. Its magnificent dome is a lasting testimony to the genius of Roman architects and as the building stands virtually intact it offers a unique opportunity for the modern visitor to step back 2,000 years and experience the glory that was Rome.
The Pantheon in Rome is able to contain a perfect sphere. The building is a cylinder 42 meter diameter with a hemispherical domed roof. The total height is 42 meter. Find the volume of the interior of the Pantheon.
items.answer:
The cylinder and the dome share the radius r = 42 ÷ 2 = 21 m. The dome is a hemisphere, so it stands 21 m tall, and since the whole building is 42 m high the cylindrical wall is 42 − 21 = 21 m high. That is why a perfect sphere of diameter 42 m fits inside.
Volume = volume of cylinder + volume of hemisphere = πr²h + (1/2)(4/3)πr³ = π(21²)(21) + (2/3)π(21³) = π(21³)(1 + 2/3) = (22/7) × 9261 × (5/3) = 22 × 21 × 21 × 5 = 48510 m³.
The interior holds about 48510 cubic metres.
items.ocr: The photograph of the Pantheon's interior is decorative; the diameter and total height are in the text, so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
DK Jain runs a company that makes ball bearings. The bearings are shipped in boxes that are then loaded onto trucks. Each bearing has a diameter of 18 mm.
(i) Each box can hold 3888π cm³ of ball bearings. How many ball bearings can a box hold?
(ii) Each ball bearing has a mass of 4 gm. Determine the mass of each box.
(iii) The maximum mass a truck can carry is 11000 kg. What is the maximum number of boxes that can be loaded into a truck?
items.answer:
(i) A bearing is a sphere of radius r = 18/2 = 9 mm, so its volume is (4/3)πr³ = (4/3)π(9³) = 972π mm³. A box holds 3888π cm³, and 1 cm³ = 1000 mm³, so the box holds 3888000π mm³. Number of bearings = 3888000π ÷ 972π = 4000.
(ii) Mass of a box = 4000 × 4 g = 16000 g = 16 kg.
(iii) A truck carries at most 11000 kg, so the number of boxes is 11000 ÷ 16 = 687.5. Boxes cannot be split, so at most 687 boxes can be loaded.
items.ocr: The stem gives the truck limit as 11000 kg, but the solution computes 12000/16 = 750 boxes. The answer above follows the printed limit of 11000 kg, which gives 687.5 and so 687 whole boxes. The photographs of ball bearings are decorative, so no figure is attached.

items.stem:
In a toys manufacturing company, wooden parts are assembled and painted to prepare a toy. For the wood processing activity center, the wood is taken out of storage to be sawed, after which it undergoes rough polishing, then is cut, drilled and has holes punched in it. It is then fine polished using sandpaper. For the retail packaging and delivery activity center, the polished wood sub-parts are assembled together, then decorated using paint.
One specific toy is in the shape of a cone mounted on a cylinder. The total height of the toy is 110 mm and the height of its conical part is 77 mm. The diameters of the base of the conical part is 72 mm and that of the cylindrical part is 40 mm.
(i) If its cylindrical part is to be painted red, what is the surface area need to be painted ?
(ii) If its conical part is to be painted blue, what is the surface area need to be painted ?
(iii) How much of the wood have been used in making the toy ?
(iv) If the cost of painting the toy is 2 paise for 8π mm², then what is the cost of painting of a box of 100 toys?
(v) If the toy manufacturer company charge 3 paise for 32π mm³ of wood, what is the price of a box of 100 toys?
items.answer:
The cone has radius r_co = 72/2 = 36 mm and height h_co = 77 mm; the cylinder has radius r_cy = 40/2 = 20 mm and height h_cy = 110 − 77 = 33 mm. The cone's slant height is l_co = √(77² + 36²) = √(5929 + 1296) = √7225 = 85 mm.
(i) The cylinder shows its curved side and its bottom face, its top being covered by the cone: 2πr_cy h_cy + πr_cy² = πr_cy(2h_cy + r_cy) = 20π(66 + 20) = 1720π mm².
(ii) The cone shows its curved side plus the ring of its base left uncovered by the narrower cylinder: πr_co l_co + π(r_co² − r_cy²) = π[36 × 85 + (1296 − 400)] = π(3060 + 896) = 3956π mm².
(iii) Wood used = volume of cone + volume of cylinder = (1/3)πr_co²h_co + πr_cy²h_cy = π[(1/3)(1296)(77) + (400)(33)] = π(33264 + 13200) = 46464π mm³.
(iv) Total painted area = 3956π + 1720π = 5676π mm². At 2 paise per 8π mm², the cost of one toy is (2 ÷ 8π) × 5676π = 1419 paise. For 100 toys: 141900 paise = Rs. 1419.
(v) At 3 paise per 32π mm³, one toy costs (3 ÷ 32π) × 46464π = 4356 paise. For a box of 100 toys: 435600 paise = Rs. 4356.
items.ocr: The printed diagram is attached: it is what shows that the cone's base (72 mm) is wider than the cylinder it stands on (40 mm), so part of the cone's base is exposed as a ring and the cylinder's top is hidden — the geometry parts (i) and (ii) turn on. The solution's line for (ii) writes πr_co l_co + πr_co² − πr_cy², the same annulus. Part (v) finishes on the following page.
